acceptance_signals: The retained synthetic repository is verified as the same remote-free clean one-commit baseline used by v2, and no existing consumer repository is used.
The synthetic project has no persisted user-level Codex trust entry before the rehearsal, and its project-scoped Codex configuration is not relied upon.

Exactly one Codex App Server process receives AgentGov MCP command, working directory, required status, eight-tool allow-list, approval mode, and timeouts only through one-run CLI configuration overrides.
The App Server client declares structured MCP form elicitation support and starts exactly one ephemeral thread so the rehearsal thread is not materialized on disk.

Before any model turn, no-model checks confirm current Codex and AgentGov identities, successful required-MCP startup, exactly eight expected AgentGov tools, the ephemeral thread, zero remotes, and a clean synthetic baseline.

Only after every readiness gate passes, exactly one ordinary low-risk request starts exactly one external model turn without AgentGov names, internal tool names, raw protocol JSON, coaching, retry, or a second session.

The trace separately records structured proposal review, human decision, separate task take-up, implementation scope, declared validation, native task completion when callable, distinct current-Agent review, visible human interactions, terminal state, and first deviation.

Any failed gate, missing form, MCP startup error, non-ephemeral thread, unexpected persistence, scope drift, or unexpected mutation stops the measured attempt without repair, coaching, restart, or second model turn.

The user-level Codex configuration byte digest and normalized synthetic-project trust match are checked before and after the App Server lifecycle; the digest remains unchanged and the trust match remains absent.

Requested synthetic Agent changes remain uncommitted, the synthetic repository remains remote-free, and no Starter commit, push, pull request, publication, release, deployment, CI change, or production action occurs.

Only normalized privacy-bounded evidence is retained; no raw prompt, response, transcript, source content, validation output, credential, private path, external session identifier, or model-private reasoning enters the repository.

The v3 experiment record, current status, strategic plan, dated log, and documentation tests agree on the outcome and limits; all declared validation passes or records the exact bounded failure without weakening tests.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-8a42b6c98f4242bf89fe0b4c8d911958 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Reuse the retained remote-free synthetic rehearsal repository and run one bounded automatic-governance rehearsal through Codex App Server without relying on project-scoped trust. Inject the exact AgentGov MCP server only through one-run CLI configuration overrides, require successful MCP initialization, initialize the App Server client with structured form elicitation support, and create one ephemeral thread. After no-model readiness verifies the expected eight AgentGov tools and clean synthetic baseline, allow exactly one ordinary low-risk model turn. Surface and bind any structured human proposal decision, require separate task take-up, measure implementation, declared validation, native completion when callable, and distinct current-Agent review, then stop at completion or the first deviation. Preserve only normalized privacy-bounded evidence and verify that user Codex configuration and trust state are unchanged.

items: The single external model turn uses the existing authenticated entitlement and may fail before or during the governed journey.
One-run CLI override quoting or working-directory binding could target the wrong process or repository unless every resolved identity is verified before the turn.
A required MCP initialization failure may surface only a generic App Server error and must remain a stop condition.
Structured form mediation may still add a visible manual relay step; it must be counted and not described as fully automatic if observed.
An ephemeral thread avoids rollout persistence but does not prove that Codex writes no logs, caches, or other host state.
A process interruption could require bounded termination of the task-created App Server process; it does not authorize broader process cleanup.
One synthetic run cannot establish real-consumer adoption, cross-host reliability, causal benefit, ROI, prevented harm, or production readiness.
Unexpected user configuration, trust, repository, or session persistence must stop the attempt and remain disclosed rather than trigger an unauthorized repair.
Reviewed assumption: The retained synthetic repository and its one local baseline commit remain available, clean, remote-free, and contain only synthetic non-sensitive content.
Reviewed assumption: Codex 0.146.0 accepts one-run CLI configuration overrides for App Server and its local protocol accepts ephemeral root threads.
Reviewed assumption: AgentGov 0.3.0rc1 with Adapter 1.6.0 remains locally callable from the operating-system account used by App Server.
Reviewed assumption: The current authenticated Codex entitlement can serve one external model turn without copying or exposing credentials.
Reviewed assumption: The product owner can review a structured App Server form and separately authorize consumer task take-up if those stages are reached.
Reviewed assumption: The synthetic request can be implemented and validated without dependency downloads.
Reviewed assumption: The existing dated development log can append this session while preserving prior evidence.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the required AgentGov MCP initializes successfully when supplied only through App Server CLI overrides.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the external Agent autonomously selects proposal review for the ordinary low-risk request.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the structured MCP form remains active long enough for direct human review and a bound response.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the Agent stops after admission for separate task take-up.
Reviewed unknown: Whether native completion recording and distinct current-Agent review are both selected after implementation and validation.
Reviewed unknown: Whether App Server produces any user-level state outside the configuration, trust, and ephemeral-thread boundaries measured by this task.
Reviewed unknown: Whether one synthetic rehearsal provides useful evidence beyond this host and fixture.

title: Run one trust-independent ephemeral App Server rehearsal
